comments.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Exempt post-build-only brief lines from the coverage rules too.** The new step 2 exemption removes a post-build Acceptance or QA line from the eval gaps. The coverage rules still treat each brief line as an item that must name an eval. A brief with a runnable Acceptance line and a separate `QA: publish a release` line therefore has no compliant coverage form: - Listing the release line with `evals: []` is refused by `coverageVerdict` before the checker runs. - Omitting the release line makes `coverageText` report a `needs-change` gap. Both paths return to the writer. After the attempt limit, the evals stage stops before implementation. Exclude a line that names only a post-build step from the coverage items and from the gap rule. Keep coverage mandatory for the testable part of a mixed line.
Suggested fix

```diff -5. Return \`coverage\` with the list. An item is one bullet or one invariant of the entry, one issue for a batch, or one line of the brief for a quick fix. Each item says in a sentence what it asks for, and names in \`evals\` the ids of the evals that cover it. A list whose coverage is missing or empty, has an item with no eval id, or names an id that is not in the list is refused. +5. Return \`coverage\` with the list. An item is one bullet or one invariant of the entry, one issue for a batch, or one line of the brief for a quick fix, except a line that names only a step after the build. Each item says in a sentence what it asks for, and names in \`evals\` the ids of the evals that cover it. A list whose coverage is missing or empty, has an item with no eval id, or names an id that is not in the list is refused. ``` ```diff -Which bullet, invariant, issue or brief line of the entry has no item? A line that names only a step after the build needs no item. Each other such gap means verdict \`needs-change\`, and you name each gap in the notes.` ```
